name: chem-r4
context:
Fourth round on a chemistry layer for a dice puzzle game. You returned REVISE last round with four findings. All were acted on and the code is now built and passing its oracle.

WHAT YOU SAID AND WHAT CHANGED:

1. You said the scoring formula was 'mathematically inverted' — 'bonds broken minus bonds formed' is delta-H, which is NEGATIVE when energy is released, so it would reward destroying bonds. Accepted in full. Score is now energy released = minus delta-H = bonds formed minus bonds broken. An oracle check asserts methane combustion comes out POSITIVE; it gives 808 kJ/mol against a textbook mean-bond-enthalpy value of roughly 802-818, and asserts the reverse reaction costs.

   Fixing the sign exposed something we had glossed: the board's tiles are FREE ATOMS, so building a molecule breaks nothing and energy released equals summed bond energy — numerically the same quantity you objected to in round 1 as 'decorative'. We concluded that objection cannot be answered by arithmetic, only by giving the player reactions between existing molecules, where bonds really are broken and delta-H can go either way. There are now two separate functions: formationEnergy (building from atoms, always positive) and reactionEnergy (rearranging, can be negative).

2. You said calling the hidden link 'a reaction pathway' was wrong because a real reaction pathway is a multidimensional coordinate in energy space, not a conduit that transports a property. Accepted. The hidden link now has NO chemical name whatsoever. A textual oracle scans the chemistry source files, comments included, and fails on VSEPR, 'molecular geometry', 'reaction pathway', 'reaction coordinate', 'transition state' and 'bond angle'.

3. You said 10.3 molecules per board was too high and made it a matching game rather than a puzzle. We re-measured properly. The 10.3 figure was an over-count: it matched regions by valence multiset rather than by actual element identity. With real elements assigned, 60 boards: 4.9 playable molecules per board, 56/60 boards have at least one, mean best-worst score spread 685 kJ/mol, and on 33 of 56 boards the best option scores at least 1.5x the median. Four boards in sixty have no playable molecule at all.

4. You called the noble-gas fix for faces 5-6 a patch. We agreed and recorded it as a known compromise rather than defending it.

ALSO BUILT: valence derived from group via min(group-10, 18-group) for groups 13-17, which gives boron 3 rather than the classroom shorthand's 5. A 16-molecule library restricted to unambiguous Lewis structures; CO, ozone, NO and NO2 are excluded on purpose because they involve formal charges, resonance or odd electron counts that would contradict the exact-valence rule the game runs on. A solver that recovers all 16 known structures from valence and adjacency alone, and refuses four plausible non-molecules.

questions.text: Is the scoring model now correct, given that formation from free atoms and summed bond energy are the same number and only reactions can go negative?
With 4.9 options per board and the best at least 1.5x the median on 59% of boards, is the scarcity now right?
Four boards in sixty have no playable molecule. Is that an acceptable dead-board rate for a puzzle game, and what should happen on those boards?
Is excluding CO, ozone, NO and NO2 from the library intellectually honest, or is it hiding chemistry that contradicts the game's rule?
What real chemistry does this design STILL teach wrongly? Be specific and name it.
